translations.text: Long ago, God spoke to our ancestors through the prophets in many portions and in many ways.
In these last days he has spoken to us through the Son, whom he appointed heir of everything, and through whom he also made the ages.
He is the radiance of God's glory and the exact likeness of his being. He sustains everything by his powerful word. After cleansing our sins, he sat down at the right hand of the Majesty on high.
He became as much greater than the angels as the name he inherited is better than theirs.
For to which of the angels did he ever say, “You are my Son; today I have fathered you”? And again, “I will be a Father to him, and he will be a Son to me.”
But when he again brings the firstborn into the world, he says, “Let all God's angels worship him.”
Of the angels he says, “He makes his angels spirits, and his servants a flame of fire.”
But to the Son he says, “Your throne, O God, is forever and ever; the scepter of your kingdom is a scepter of uprightness.
You loved righteousness and hated lawlessness. Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions.”
And, “You, Lord, founded the earth in the beginning, and the heavens are the work of your hands.
They will perish, but you endure and remain; they will all wear out like clothes.
You will roll them up like a cloak, like a garment, and they will be rolled up. But you remain the same, and your years will not come to an end.”
To which of the angels did he ever say, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet”?
Are they not all spirits in service, sent to minister for the sake of those who will inherit salvation?
Therefore we must pay even closer attention to the words that have been spoken, so that we never drift away.
For if the word spoken through angels proved firm, and every transgression and act of disobedience received a penalty of punishment,
how will we escape if we neglect so great a salvation? It was first spoken by the Lord and was confirmed to us by those who heard him,
with God bearing witness through signs and wonders, various mighty works, and distributions of the Holy Spirit according to his own will.
For he did not subject the world to come, about which we are speaking, to angels.
Someone testified somewhere, saying, “What is a human being that you remember him, or a son of man that you care for him?
You made him a little lower than the angels; you crowned him with glory and honor and placed him over the works of your hands.
You subjected everything under his feet.” Now, in subjecting everything to him, he left nothing that was not subject to him. But at present we do not yet see everything subjected to him.
But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death, so that by God's grace he might taste death for everyone.
For it was fitting that he, for whom everything exists and through whom everything exists, in bringing many sons to glory, should make the leader of their salvation perfect through sufferings.
For the one who sanctifies and those who are sanctified were all from one source. For this reason he is not ashamed to call them brothers and to say,
I will proclaim your name to my brothers; in the midst of the assembly I will praise you.
And again: “I will put my trust in him.” And again: “Here I am, and the children whom God has given me.”
Now, since the children shared in blood and flesh, he himself likewise shared in those same things, so that through his death he might destroy the one who held the power of death, that is, Satan,
and free those who were continually held in slavery by the fear of death.
For he never takes hold of angels, but takes hold of Abraham’s descendants.
Therefore he had to become like his brothers in every way, so that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in matters relating to God, to make atonement for the sins of the people.
For because he himself suffered when put to the test, he is able to help those who are being tested.
Therefore, holy brothers, who share in the heavenly calling, consider Jesus Christ, the apostle and high priest of our confession,
who is faithful to his maker, just as Moses was in all his house.
For he was considered worthy of greater glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house has greater honor than the house.
For every house is built by someone, but the one who made everything is God.
Moses is faithful in all his house as a servant, as a testimony to the things that would be spoken,
but Christ as a son over his own house. We ourselves are his house, if only we hold firmly to our confidence and our boasting in hope until the end.
Therefore the Holy Spirit says this: “Today, if you hear his voice,
do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion, on the day of testing in the wilderness,
where your fathers tested me, put me to the proof, and saw my works for forty years.
Therefore I was disgusted with that generation and said, ‘They always go astray in their hearts.’ And they did not know my ways.”
As I swore in my anger, “They shall not enter my rest.”
Take care, brothers, lest any of you ever have an evil, unbelieving heart that turns away from the living God.
Instead, encourage one another every day, while today is still before you, so that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
For we have become sharers in Christ, if only we hold our initial confidence firmly to the end.
When it is said, “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion.”
For some heard and rebelled, but not all who came out of Egypt through Moses.
With whom was he disgusted for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bones fell there in the wilderness?
To whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest, if not to those who did not believe?
And we see that they could not enter because of their unbelief.
Therefore let us be afraid, lest, while the promise of entering his rest remains, any of you should be found to have fallen short.
For we have received the good news just as they did, but hearing the word did them no good, since they were not united in the obedience of faith.
But we who have believed enter the rest, just as he said, “As I swore in my anger, ‘They shall not enter my rest,’” although the works had been completed since the beginning of the world.
For somewhere he speaks about the seventh day in this way: “And God rested on the seventh day from all his works.”
And here again he says, “They shall not enter my rest.”
Now, since some were prevented from entering it, and those who had previously received the good news did not enter because of their disobedience,
he again appoints another day, “Today,” speaking through David after so long a time, as he said before: “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts.”
For if Joshua had given them rest, he would not afterward have spoken about another day.
Thus, a Sabbath rest has been diminished for the people of God.
For whoever has entered his rest has also rested from his own works, just as God did from his.
Let us therefore strive to enter that rest, so that no one falls by the same example of disobedience.

For the word of God is living and active and sharper than any two-edged sword. It penetrates as far as the division of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and judges the thoughts and intentions of hearts.
And no creature is invisible before him, but everything lies naked before the eyes of him about whom we are speaking.
Since we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold firmly to our confession.
For we do not have a high priest who is unable to share in our weakness, but one who has been tested in every way as we are, without sin.
Let us therefore approach his throne of grace boldly, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help at the proper time.
For every high priest taken from among human beings stands on their behalf in matters concerning God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins.
He can share with moderation in the suffering of the ignorant and those who have gone astray, because he himself is clothed in weakness.
For this reason, he must offer sacrifices for sins for himself as well as for the people.
And no one takes this honor for himself, but only one who is called by God, as Aaron was.
Likewise, Christ did not glorify himself by becoming high priest, but the one who said to him, “You are my Son; today I have begotten you.”
As he also says in another place, “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”
In the days of his flesh, he offered prayers and supplications, with loud cries and tears, to the one who could save him from death, and he was heard because of his goodness.
Although he is a Son, he learned obedience through suffering.
And when he was made perfect, he became the source of eternal salvation for all who obey him,
and he was named by God a high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
We have much to say about this, and it is difficult to explain, because you have become dull in hearing.
For although by this time you ought to be teachers, you again need to be taught the elementary principles of God's words, and you have come to need milk rather than solid food.
For everyone who feeds on milk is unfamiliar with the word of righteousness, because he is a child.
But solid food is for the mature, whose senses, because they have reached maturity, are trained to distinguish good and evil.
Therefore, leaving the elementary teaching about Christ, let us move on to maturity, not laying again a foundation of repentance from dead works and of faith in God,
and of teaching about baptisms, the laying on of hands, the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.
And we will do this if God permits.
For it is impossible for those who have once been baptized, who have tasted the heavenly gift and have shared in the Holy Spirit,
and have tasted the goodness of God's word and the powers of the world to come,
and then fall away, to be renewed again to repentance, as they crucify the Son of God again for themselves and expose him to disgrace again.
For land that drinks the rain that often falls upon it and produces crops useful to those for whom it is cultivated receives a blessing from God.
But land that produces thorns and thistles is worthless and near to being cursed, and its end is burning.
But I am convinced of better things concerning you, beloved, things that belong to salvation, even though we speak in this way.
For God is not unjust so as to forget your works and the love you show toward his name, because you served the saints and continue to serve them.
And we desire that each of you show the same diligence in the assurance of hope until the end,
so that you do not become sluggish, but become imitators of those who through faith and patience inherited the promise.
For when God made the promise to Abraham, since there was no one greater by whom he could swear,
he swore by himself and said, “Yes, I will surely bless you and surely multiply you.”
And so, having been patient, he obtained the promise.
Indeed, people swear by someone greater than themselves, and an oath serves as confirmation to settle every dispute among them.
Therefore God, wishing all the more to show the heirs of the promise the unchangeableness of his purpose, intervened with an oath,
so that through two unchangeable things, in which it is impossible for God to lie, we who have taken refuge might have firm encouragement to grasp the hope set before us,
We have this as a firm and immovable anchor for our souls, which also enters the inner sanctuary behind the curtain.
where Jesus, our forerunner, entered on our behalf, having become a high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
For this Melchizedek was king of Salem, priest of God Most High, who went out to meet Abraham when he was returning from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him.
Abraham also gave him a tenth of everything. His name is translated first as “king of righteousness,” and then he is king of Salem, which means “king of peace.”
Without father, without mother, not reckoned in a genealogy, having neither a beginning of days nor an end of life, but resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever.
Now see how great this man was, to whom even the patriarch Abraham gave a tenth of the spoils.

Those of the sons of Levi who receive the priesthood have a commandment under the law to collect a tenth from the people, that is, from their own brothers, although they too have come from the loins of Abraham.
But the one whose ancestry was not counted among them collected a tenth from Abraham and blessed the one who had received the promise.
Without any dispute, the lesser is blessed by the greater.
Here, mortal men receive tenths, but there, the one who receives them is testified to be alive.
And, so to speak, even Levi, who received tenths, paid a tenth through Abraham,
for he was still in his father's loins when Melchizedek met him.

Now if perfection came through the Levitical priesthood—for under it the people received the law—what need was there for another priest to arise according to the order of Melchizedek, rather than to be called a priest according to the order of Aaron?
But when the priesthood changes, the law must also change.
For the one of whom these things are said belonged to a different tribe, from which no one ever served at the altar.
For it is clear that our Lord arose from the tribe of Judah, and Moses said nothing about priests from that tribe.
And it is even clearer that another priest will arise in the likeness of Melchizedek,
who became a priest not according to a commandment concerning the flesh, but according to the power of an endless life.
For it was testified, “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”
The former commandment was set aside because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law made nothing perfect, and a better hope was introduced, through which we draw near to God.
And this was not without an oath, for some became priests without an oath,
but he became a priest with an oath through the one who said to him, “The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind: You are a priest forever.”
To that extent, Jesus became the guarantor of a better covenant.
And many became priests because death prevented them from continuing forever.
But because he remains forever, he holds his priesthood permanently.
Therefore he is also able to save completely those who come to God through him, since he always lives to intercede for them.
For such a high priest was indeed fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, separated from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.
He does not need, like the other high priests, to offer sacrifices daily, first for their own sins and then for those of the people. He did this once for all when he offered himself as a sacrifice.
The law appoints as high priests men subject to weakness, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appoints the Son, who has been made perfect forever.
Now the main point of what we are saying is this: we have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of the Majesty in heaven,
a minister of the holy places and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord set up, not a human being.
For every high priest stands to offer sacrifices and offerings; therefore he too must have something to offer.
For if he were on earth, perhaps he would not even be a priest, since there were those who offered gifts according to the law,

who served a representation and a copy of the heavenly things, just as Moses was instructed when he was about to make the tent of worship. “See,” he says, “that you make everything according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain.”
But now Jesus has obtained a more excellent ministry, just as he is also the mediator of a better covenant, which was established on better promises.
For if the first covenant had been faultless, no place would have been sought for a second.
But he finds fault with them and says, “Look, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will establish a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah,

not like the covenant I made with their fathers on the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of the land of the Egyptians. For they did not remain in my covenant, and I disregarded them, says the Lord Almighty.

But this is the covenant I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws into their minds and write them on their hearts. I will be their God, and they will be my people.
And they will no longer each teach their fellow citizen or their brother, saying, ‘Know the Lord,’ for they will all know me, from the least to the greatest among them,
because I will be merciful toward their injustices, and I will no longer remember their sins and their lawless deeds.”
Now, by saying “new,” he has made the first covenant old. And what is growing old and aging is near destruction.
The first covenant also had regulations for worship at that time, and an earthly sanctuary.
For the first tent was furnished in this way: in it were the lampstand, the table, and the bread of the offering. It was called the Holy Place.
And behind the second curtain was the tent called the Holy of Holies,

in which were the golden censer and the ark of the covenant, covered inside and outside with gold. In it were the golden jar full of manna, Aaron’s rod that blossomed, and the tablets of the covenant.
Above it were the cherubim of glory, overshadowing the mercy seat. We cannot now speak of these things one by one.
When all these things had been arranged in this way, the priests entered the first tent continually to perform the services of worship,
but only the high priest entered the second, once a year, and not without blood, which he offered for himself and for the people’s sins committed in ignorance.
By this the Holy Spirit showed that the way into the sanctuary had not yet been revealed, because the first tent still remained in place.
It is a symbol of the time then present, in which offerings and sacrifices were presented that could not make the worshipers perfect in conscience, but concerned only food and drink
and various washings—regulations for the body imposed until the time of reform.
But Christ came as high priest of the good things to come, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by human hands—that is, not belonging to this creation.
And he entered the sanctuary once, not with the blood of goats and calves, but with his own blood, having obtained eternal redemption.
For if the blood of bulls and goats and the ashes of heifers sprinkled on the defiled sanctified them so that their bodies were clean,
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself as an unblemished sacrifice to God, cleanse your conscience from dead works to serve the living God!

And for this reason he is the mediator of a new covenant, so that, when a death takes place to redeem the transgressions committed under the first covenant, those who have been called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.
For where there is a will, the death of the person who made it must be established.
For a will is valid after death; otherwise, how could it be valid while the person who made it is alive?
Therefore even the first covenant was not inaugurated without blood.

For when Moses had recounted every commandment of the law to the people, he took the blood of bulls and goats, with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book of the covenant itself and all the people.
And he said, “This is the blood of the covenant that God commanded for you.”
And he likewise sprinkled the tabernacle and all the vessels used in service with blood.
And according to the law, almost everything was purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood there was no forgiveness.
It was therefore necessary for the representations to be purified with such things, but the heavenly things themselves with better sacrifices than these.
For Christ did not enter holy places made by human hands, copies of the true ones, but heaven itself, to appear before the face of God on our behalf.
Nor was it so that he might offer himself as a sacrifice many times, as the high priest entered the Holy of Holies year after year with another’s blood.
Otherwise he would have had to suffer many times since the beginning of the world. But now, at the end of the ages, he has appeared once to do away with sins through his own sacrifice.
And just as it is appointed for human beings to die once, and after that comes judgment,
so Christ, having been offered once as a sacrifice to take away the sins of many, will appear a second time, without sin, for the salvation of those who await him in faith.
For the law had a shadow of the good things to come, not the actual form of those things. Year after year they offer the same sacrifices [?], which cannot make perfect those who approach.
Otherwise they would have stopped offering them, because the worshipers, once purified, would no longer have any consciousness of sin.
Instead, in those very sacrifices there was a reminder of sins year after year,
for the blood of goats and bulls could not take away sins.
For this reason, when he enters the world, he says, “You did not desire sacrifices and offerings, but you prepared a body for me.
You took no pleasure in burnt offerings and offerings for sins.
Then I said, ‘Here I am; I have come—in the scroll of the book it is written about me—to do your will, O God.’”
He says above, “You were not pleased with and did not desire sacrifices, offerings, burnt offerings, and offerings for sin,” which were offered according to the law.
Then he says, “Here I am; I come to do your will, O God.” He rejects the first in order to establish the second.
By that will we too have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once.
And every high priest stands daily in service and offers the same sacrifices many times, which can never take away sins.
But he offered one sacrifice for sins and sat down forever at the right hand of God.
And from then on he waits until his enemies are placed beneath his feet.
For by one sacrifice he has perfected forever those who have been sanctified.
The Holy Spirit also testifies to us, after first saying:
“This is the covenant that I will make with their fathers after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws in their minds, and I will write them in their thoughts.”
Then he says, “I will no longer remember their sins and their lawless deeds.”
Now where there is forgiveness, there is no longer any need for a sacrifice for sins.
Therefore, brothers, we have confidence to enter the holy places by the blood of Jesus,
by the new and living way that he opened for us through the curtain, that is, his flesh,
and we have a great priest over the house of God.
Let us draw near with sincere hearts in the fullness of faith, our hearts washed clean of an evil conscience and our bodies baptized in the water of sanctification.
Let us hold firmly to the confession of our hope without wavering, for the one who promised is faithful.
And let us be attentive to one another, encouraging love and good works.
Let us not abandon our gatherings together, as some are accustomed to doing, but let us encourage one another, all the more as you see the day approaching.
For if we sin deliberately after receiving the knowledge of the truth, a sacrifice for sins is no longer of any use.
Instead, there is a fearful expectation of judgment and the fury of fire that will consume the adversaries.
Anyone who disregarded the law of Moses died without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.

How much more severe a punishment do you think someone deserves who has trampled the Son of God underfoot, regarded as common the blood of the new covenant by which he was sanctified, and insulted the Spirit of grace?
For we know the one who said, “Vengeance is mine, and I will repay, says the Lord.” And again, “The Lord will judge his people.”
It is a terrible thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
Now remember the former days, when, after being enlightened, you endured many struggles and sufferings,
sometimes publicly exposed to insults and afflictions, and sometimes becoming companions of those who suffered in this way.
For you also suffered with the prisoners and joyfully accepted the plundering of your possessions, because you knew that you yourselves had better possessions in heaven, where they endure and remain.
Therefore, do not cast away your confidence, which carries a great reward.
You need endurance so that, after doing the will of God, you may receive what was promised.
For in just a very little while, the one who is to come will come and will not delay.
For my righteous one will live by faith, and if anyone wavers, my soul will take no pleasure in him.
But we are not among those who waver and perish, but among those who have faith and save their souls.
What is faith but the assurance of things hoped for and the evidence of things not seen?
For by it those of old received approval.
By faith we understand that the ages were established by the word of God, and that visible things came into being from invisible things.

By faith Abel offered God better offerings than Cain, through which he received testimony that he was righteous, for God testified to him concerning his offerings. Though he died, through that same faith he still speaks.

By faith Enoch was taken away so that he would not taste death, and he could not be found anywhere, because God had taken him away. Before he was taken away, he received testimony that he was pleasing to God.
But without faith it is impossible to please him. Whoever approaches God must believe that God exists and that he rewards those who seek him.

By faith Noah, receiving instructions about things not yet seen, was moved by fear and built the ark to save his household. Through this he condemned the world and became an heir of the righteousness that comes through faith.
By faith Abraham, when he was called, obeyed and went out to the place he was to receive as an inheritance. He set out without knowing where he was going.
By faith he lived as a stranger in the land of promise, as in a foreign country, dwelling in tents with Isaac and Jacob, who were fellow heirs of the same promise.
For he was looking forward to the city established on foundations, whose architect and maker is God.
By faith Sarah herself, who was barren, received the power to conceive a child and gave birth when she was past the proper age, because she considered the one who had promised to be faithful.
Therefore from one man, who was himself past the proper age, descendants were born as numerous as the stars of heaven and as countless as the sand on the seashore.
All these died in faith without yet receiving the promises, but they saw them from afar and rejoiced, and acknowledged that they were foreigners and strangers on the earth.
For those who say such things make it clear that they are seeking a homeland.
If they had been thinking of the land from which they had departed, they would have had time to return there.
But as it is, they long for a better land, that is, a heavenly one. Therefore God is not ashamed to be called their God, for he has prepared a city for them.
By faith Abraham offered Isaac as a sacrifice when he was tested. He who had received the promises was offering his only son,
to whom it had been said, “Through Isaac your descendants will be named.”
He considered that God was able even to raise the dead, and from there he received him back, figuratively speaking.
By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning things to come.
By faith Jacob, as he was dying, blessed each of Joseph’s sons and bowed in worship over the top of his staff.
By faith Joseph, at his death, spoke of the departure of the sons of Israel and gave instructions concerning his own bones.
By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, because they saw that the child was beautiful, and they were not afraid of the king’s command.
By faith Moses, when he grew up, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter.
He considered it better to suffer with the people of God than to enjoy sin for a short time.
He considered the reproach of Christ more valuable than the great treasures of the Egyptians, for he looked ahead to the payment of the reward.
By faith he left the land of the Egyptians and did not fear the king’s anger, for he persevered, regarding the unseen as though he could see it.
By faith he observed the Passover and the pouring out of blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not come near them.
By faith they crossed the Red Sea as though crossing dry land; when the Egyptians attempted this, they drowned.
By faith the walls of Jericho fell after they had marched around them for seven days.
By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with the unbelievers, because she had welcomed the spies in peace.
And now, what more shall I say? There is not enough time for me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and the other prophets,
who through faith conquered kingdoms, practiced righteousness, obtained promises, and shut the mouths of lions.
They quenched the power of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were strengthened out of weakness, became mighty in battle, and captured the armies of foreigners.
Women received their dead back through resurrection. Others were tortured and did not accept deliverance, so that they might attain a better resurrection.
Others experienced tortures and beatings, chains and imprisonment.
They were stoned, sawn apart, put to the test, and killed with the sword. They wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, afflicted, and tormented.
The world was not worthy of them. They wandered in deserts and mountains, in caves and holes in the earth.
And all these, though commended for their faith, did not receive what was promised,
because God had provided something better for us, so that they would not be made perfect without us.
Therefore, since we too have such a great multitude of witnesses gathered around us, let us cast off all pride and burdensome sins, and let us run with endurance in the contest set before us.
Let us look to Jesus, the leader and perfecter of faith, who, in exchange for the joy set before him, accepted the cross, despised its shame, and sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
Consider him who endured such opposition from sinners, so that you do not grow weary in your souls and lose heart.
For in your struggle against sin, you have not yet resisted to the point of shedding blood.
And you have forgotten the encouragement that speaks to you as to children: “My child, do not lose heart under the Lord’s discipline, and do not be discouraged when he rebukes you.
For the Lord disciplines those he loves and punishes every child he accepts.”
Endure discipline; God deals with you as sons. What son is there whom his father does not discipline?
For if you are without discipline, in which everyone has shared, then you are illegitimate children and not sons.
For if we respect our earthly fathers, whom we have as disciplinarians, how much more should we submit to the Father of spirits and live?
For they discipline us for a short time according to their own wishes, but he does so for our benefit, so that we may share in his holiness.
All discipline seems at the time to bring sorrow rather than joy, but afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those trained by it.
Therefore strengthen your drooping hands and weak knees,
and make straight paths for your feet, so that what is lame may not stumble and fall, but rather be healed.
Pursue peace with everyone, and holiness, without which no one will see the Lord.
Be careful that no one falls short of the grace of God, and that no root of bitterness springs up to cause trouble and defile many through it.
Let no one be sexually immoral or unholy like Esau, who sold his birthright for a single meal.
You know that although he later wanted to inherit the blessing, he was rejected, for he found no opportunity for repentance, even though he sought it with tears.
For you have not approached a mountain that could be touched, which burned with fire and was covered with mist, fog, darkness, and gloom,
where a trumpet sounded and a voice spoke words, so that those who heard begged that the message not be repeated to them.
For they could not bear the command: even if an animal approached the mountain, it was to be stoned.
And the sight was so terrifying that even Moses said, “I am struck with fear and trembling.”
But you have approached Mount Zion and the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and countless hosts of angels,
and the assembly of the firstborn enrolled in heaven, and God, the judge of all, and the spirits of the righteous made perfect,
and Jesus, the mediator of the new covenant, and the outpouring of his blood, which speaks more powerfully than Abel’s.
Be careful not to refuse the one who spoke. For if those who refused the one who gave commands on earth could not escape, how much less will we escape if we turn our backs on the one from heaven?
His voice shook the earth then, but now he has promised, saying, “Once more I will shake not only the earth but also the heavens.”
The words “once more” indicate the removal of the things that can be shaken, as things that have been made, so that the things that cannot be shaken may remain firm.
Therefore, receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us hold firmly to grace, through which we serve God acceptably, with fear and trembling.
For our God is a consuming fire.
Let brotherly love remain firm among you.
Do not forget hospitality to strangers, for through it some have received angels without knowing it.
Remember those in chains as though you were bound with them, and those who are mistreated, since you yourselves also have bodies.
Marriage is honorable in every way, and the marriage bed is pure, but God judges adulterers and the sexually immoral.
Let your conduct be free from the love of money, being content with whatever you have, for he himself said, “I will not leave you or cast you aside.”
So we may boldly say, “The Lord is my helper, and I will not be afraid. What can a human being do to me?”
Remember your leaders, who spoke the word of God to you. Consider the outcome of their lives and imitate their faith.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
Do not be led astray by various and strange teachings, for it is good for hearts to be strengthened by grace, not by foods, which did not benefit those who followed such practices.
We have an altar from which those who serve in the tabernacle have no right to eat.
For the bodies of the animals whose blood was brought into the sanctuary by the high priest for sins were burned outside the camp.
For this reason Jesus also suffered outside the gate, so that he might sanctify the people by his own blood.
Therefore, come, let us go out to him outside the camp, bearing his disgrace.
For we do not have a city here that will endure, but we seek the one to come.
Therefore, through him let us continually offer God a sacrifice of praise, that is, the fruit of lips that confess his name.
Do not forget to do good and to share, for God is pleased with such sacrifices.

Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they keep watch over your souls as those who will give an account concerning you. Let them do this with joy and not with sighing, for that would be of no benefit to you.
Pray for us, for we know with confidence that we have a good conscience, and we wish to conduct ourselves well in everything.
And I urge you all the more to do this, so that I may be restored to you sooner.
And the God of peace, who brought up from the dead the great Shepherd of the flocks, our Lord Jesus, by the blood of the eternal covenant,
May he strengthen you in good works to do his will, and may he work in us what is pleasing in his sight through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever. Amen.
I urge you, brothers, to listen to this word of encouragement, for I have written to you briefly.
Know that our brother Timothy has been released to you. If he comes soon, I will see you with him.
Greet all your leaders and all the saints. Those in the regions of Italy greet you.
Grace be with you all. To the Hebrews, written from Italy through Timothy.
